subject: Recap: Discovery + Exec sponsor intro — Acme Health
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Reynolds <sophie.reynolds@acmehealth.com>, Mark Chen <mark.chen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-18T16:02:00Z
Subject: Recap: Discovery + Exec sponsor intro — Acme Health

Hi Sophie / Mark —

Thanks again for the time today — appreciated the candid conversation and for introducing the exec sponsors. Quick recap of what we heard and agreed: 

Key pain points
- Unpredictable inference cost spikes tied to high-volume clinical workflows (overnight batch and daytime peaks).
- Latency in the clinical UI: current model endpoints exceed your 95th percentile target during peak shifts (impacts clinician throughput).
- Security/regulatory: need clear controls for PHI, SOC 2 + BAA, and VPC/on-prem options for certain workflows.

Goals (what success looks like)
- Reduce per-inference unit cost by ~30-40% while maintaining or improving response quality for triage prompts.
- Meet latency SLO: 95th < 200ms for interactive flows.
- Private deployment option (VPC or on-prem) for PHI-sensitive pipelines and documented BAA/SOC2 evidence.

Immediate next steps we agreed
1) Redwood to send a concise executive-level recap + proposed mutual action plan (attached MAP 1-pager).
2) Security questionnaire & SOC2 artifacts (we attached a template and can follow up with SOC2/BAA docs once we have NDA).
3) Pilot scope: 6–8 week pilot scoped to 2 clinical workflows; target metrics + success criteria defined by your clinical lead.
4) Procurement timeline: Mark to share procurement contact and target decision window (you mentioned end of Q2).

Attachments: Redwood-ACME-MAP-1-pager.pdf, security-questionnaire-template.docx

If I missed anything obvious, call it out — otherwise I’ll prepare the MAP and loop in Marissa to run pricing and pilot scoping.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | (415) 555-0124

--
Redwood Inference | Developer-first inference for production

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-19T08:10:00Z
Subject: Exec recap & ask: Acme Health discovery — business outcomes, risks, procurement path

Team —

TL;DR: High-potential account (Acme Health) with exec sponsor and procurement in process. Pilot + potential Dedicated/Private deployment depending on security/PHI scoping. Requesting support on pricing flexibility and SOC2/BAA turnaround.

What we heard (business outcomes)
- Outcome they care about: faster clinician throughput and predictable inference spend tied to per-encounter economics. If we can hit cost + latency targets, they will consider a Dedicated pool or Private deployment for PHI flows.
- Potential contract: pilot -> rollout to ~3 internal apps -> Dedicated capacity for PHI workflows. Could expand across 3 hospital networks (TAM ~$500k ARR year 1, expansion upside).

Key risks / blockers
- Compliance & legal: BAA required; they will need SOC2 artifacts and likely an onsite/attestation conversation for certain partners.
- Procurement timeline: PO expected by end of Q2; procurement may request net-60 terms and additional attestations.
- Latency SLO: they want 95th < 200ms for interactive flows — may require GPU placement in their preferred region or Dedicated capacity / reserved CPU/GPU profile.

Asks from leadership
1) Pricing: approval for a pilot credit and a temporary pricing concession if they commit to Dedicated within 6 months. I suggest we budget a $25k pilot credit (sales/ops approval pending).
2) Security: Marissa — can you own SOC2/BAA artifact delivery and coordinate with Security for any follow-up?
3) Solutions: Dylan — lead the pilot scoping and produce an initial architecture note (VPC vs Dedicated) and expected latency profile.
4) Escalation: if procurement pushes for net-60 or extended warranties, escalate to Finance + Legal — we may need Ops to confirm SLA fallback options.

Attachments: pricing-term-sheet.xlsx (draft numbers, including pilot credit scenarios)

I’ll set up a follow-up internal sync for Monday to triage next steps and lock owners.

Thanks —
Aditya
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-19T09:24:00Z
Subject: Re: Exec recap & ask: Acme Health discovery — business outcomes, risks, procurement path

Aditya / Marissa —

Good write-up. I approve moving forward with the pilot credit (budget up to $25k) and a temporary pricing concession contingent on a Dedicated commitment within 6 months. Marissa — please lead contract/procurement engagement and coordinate with Security on the BAA/SOC2 artifacts.

Dylan — please prioritize the architecture note; highlight options for Dedicated vs VPC and any ramp-up time that impacts latency. Include estimated infra cost delta if we place capacity in the customer-preferred region.

Finance/Legal note: expect procurement to ask for net-60. We should push for net-30 or milestone-based payments tied to pilot acceptance. If procurement insists on net-60, escalate to me and Finance.

Vivek Kulkarni
Chief Revenue Officer | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
